location.basis: Centre of the walled enclosure read on the imagery (about 25.4985 N, 61.9503 E), 160 m south-west of the published Wikipedia position 25.49992 N, 61.95088 E, on the east bank of the Dasht river valley in Pakistani Makran.

systems.part: walled enclosure ('citadel') at the published site position

main_system_reason: The only straight lines we found are the west and east sides of the walled enclosure; they are parallel within their errors and form the only system.
notes: The Esri imagery is a Vantor Vivid mosaic of 3 April 2025 with real detail to zoom 18 (0.54 m per pixel). At the published position a reddish, rubble-strewn area of about 110 x 150 m is bounded on the west and east by straight pale bands, which we read as the collapsed stone walls of the enclosure that Stein and Dales described as the citadel; its north side is diffuse and its south side runs into gullies, so we measured only the west and east sides. The identification of the bands as walls rests on their straightness, their parallel course and their position at the site, not on visible masonry, so both lines are low-confidence; on this rocky terrace a natural ledge could produce a similar edge. The west band has a sharp outer edge over 145 m, the east band only a softer edge over 97 m.
